review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

22:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λέγων
22:1.targetText: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables:

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν, "answering, said", is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγων ("saying") only introduces the parable; BSB uses a colon.

22:2.sourceText: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ, ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ.
22:2.targetText: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

groups.note: The aorist passive Ὡμοιώθη, "has been likened", is rendered is like.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the apposition ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ (a man, a king) simply as a king.

22:3.sourceText: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν.
22:3.targetText: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.

groups.note: The article with the passive participle, "the invited ones", is rendered actively with the king as subject.
οὐκ ἤθελον, "they were not willing", is rendered they refused.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:4.sourceText: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα, οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα, καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα· δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
22:4.targetText: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the invited ones", is rendered those who have been invited.
One participle τεθυμένα serves both oxen and cattle.

unmappedSource.reason: Ἰδού ("look") is not expressed; BSB turns the message into an indirect statement.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle λέγων is rendered as the finite verb said.
English introduces the message as an indirect statement; the Greek has direct speech.
English supplies the copula; the Greek has πάντα ἕτοιμα without a verb.

22:5.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον, ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν, ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ·
22:5.targetText: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.

groups.note: In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
ὃς μέν … ὃς δέ is the Greek idiom for one … another.
ἴδιον ("own") is rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀμελήσαντες is rendered as the finite verb paid no attention.

22:6.sourceText: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
22:6.targetText: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the object; τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ("his servants") serves all three verbs.
English repeats the object; τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ("his servants") serves all three verbs.

22:7.sourceText: ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη, καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν.
22:7.targetText: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.

groups.note: The finite verb ἀπώλεσεν ("destroyed") is rendered as the purpose of sent.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:8.sourceText: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·
22:8.targetText: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.

groups.note: The article with the passive participle, "the invited ones", is rendered actively with the king as subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed; the contrast is carried by but (δέ).

22:9.sourceText: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
22:9.targetText: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’

groups.note: διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, "the outlets of the roads", is rendered crossroads.
ὅσους ἐάν is one indefinite relative, "as many as".

22:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ νυμφὼν ἀνακειμένων.
22:10.targetText: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

unmappedSource.reason: The demonstrative ἐκεῖνοι ("those") is not separately expressed; BSB has the servants.
The relative οὕς ("whom") is left implicit in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθόντες is rendered as the finite verb went out.

22:11.sourceText: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·
22:11.targetText: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

groups.note: The participle εἰσελθών is rendered as a when-clause.
The participle ἐνδεδυμένον is rendered as a relative clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverb ἐκεῖ ("there") is not separately expressed in this English wording.

22:12.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου; ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.
22:12.targetText: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’  But the man was speechless.

groups.note: μὴ ἔχων, "not having", is rendered without.
In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB says the man.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί before λέγει is not expressed; BSB places he asked after the address.
BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

22:13.sourceText: τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
22:13.targetText: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

groups.note: The participle Δήσαντες is rendered as a command beside throw.
The possessive αὐτοῦ ("his" feet and hands) becomes the object him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle Δήσαντες is rendered as the command Tie.

22:14.sourceText: Πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.
22:14.targetText: For many are called, but few are chosen.”

groups.note: One εἰσιν serves both clauses; English repeats are.

22:15.sourceText: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.
22:15.targetText: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.

groups.note: συμβούλιον ἔλαβον, "took counsel", is rendered conspired.
ὅπως with the subjunctive expresses purpose, rendered to.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered with the name.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle πορευθέντες is rendered as the finite verb went out.
English supplies the possessive; the Greek has ἐν λόγῳ ("in speech") alone.

22:16.sourceText: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντας Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·
22:16.targetText: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.

groups.note: οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, "you are not concerned about anyone", is rendered You seek favor from no one.
The Greek double negative οὐ … οὐδενός makes a single English negative.
πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, "the face of men", is rendered external appearance.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; BSB starts a new sentence.

22:17.sourceText: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν, τί σοι δοκεῖ; ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;
22:17.targetText: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

22:18.sourceText: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;
22:18.targetText: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle γνούς is rendered as the finite verb knew.

22:19.sourceText: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου. οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον.
22:19.targetText: Show Me the coin used for the tax.”  And they brought Him a denarius.

groups.note: The genitive article τοῦ, "of the", is rendered used for the.
In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.

22:20.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;
22:20.targetText: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”

groups.note: One Τίνος serves both nouns; English repeats whose.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί before λέγει is not expressed; BSB places He asked after the question.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:21.sourceText: λέγουσιν· Καίσαρος. τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ.
22:21.targetText: “Caesar’s,” they answered.  So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

groups.note: The neuter article τά, "the things", is rendered what.
The neuter article τά, "the things", is rendered what.

English supplies the copula; τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ is literally "the things of God".

22:22.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.
22:22.targetText: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a when-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard; the Greek has none.
English coordinator; the participle ἀφέντες is rendered as the finite verb left.

22:23.sourceText: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
22:23.targetText: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered with the name.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition ἐν is absorbed in the English time phrase.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds same for emphasis; the Greek has ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ("that day").

22:24.sourceText: λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
22:24.targetText: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.

groups.note: τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ, "for his brother", is rendered for him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The possessive αὐτοῦ ("his") is not rendered; BSB calls her the widow.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds that before the reported law; the Greek has no ὅτι.

22:25.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·
22:25.targetText: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.

groups.note: The καί before μὴ ἔχων … ἀφῆκεν introduces the consequence, rendered So.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί is not expressed; BSB starts a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds one after the ordinal first.
English coordinator; the participle γήμας is rendered as the finite verb married.

22:26.sourceText: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·
22:26.targetText: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.

groups.note: ἕως τῶν ἑπτά, "up to the seven", is rendered down to the seventh.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the elliptical Greek; ὁμοίως means "likewise".
English supplies the noun the ordinals imply.

22:27.sourceText: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή.
22:27.targetText: And last of all, the woman died.

22:28.sourceText: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή; πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.
22:28.targetText: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”

22:29.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
22:29.targetText: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν, "answering, said", is rendered by one verb.
The participle εἰδότες is rendered as a causal clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

22:30.sourceText: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν.
22:30.targetText: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

groups.note: The present γαμοῦσιν ("they marry") is rendered as a future with people as subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The explanatory γάρ ("for") is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:31.sourceText: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγοντος
22:31.targetText: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:

groups.note: τὸ ῥηθέν, "the thing spoken", is rendered what … said, with God as subject.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns the passive "spoken by God" into the active God said; ὑπό and the article have no separate counterpart.
The participle λέγοντος ("saying") only introduces the quotation.

22:32.sourceText: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰακώβ; οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων.
22:32.targetText: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

unmappedSource.reason: The καί between the first two names is not rendered; English uses a comma.

22:33.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
22:33.targetText: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard; the Greek has none.

22:34.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους, συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό,
22:34.targetText: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a when-clause.
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, "at the same place", is one idiom for together.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐφίμωσεν.

22:35.sourceText: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν
22:35.targetText: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:

groups.note: The finite verb ἐπηρώτησεν ("asked") is rendered with a question, while the participle πειράζων becomes the main verb tested.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

22:36.sourceText: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;
22:36.targetText: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

groups.note: The positive μεγάλη ("great") has superlative force here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek question has no verb.

22:37.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου.
22:37.targetText: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Jesus.
The future Ἀγαπήσεις ("you shall love") is rendered as the command Love.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

22:38.targetText: This is the first and greatest commandment.

22:39.sourceText: δευτέρα ὁμοία αὐτῇ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
22:39.targetText: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no δέ here; BSB's And matches the reading δευτέρα δέ found in other editions.

22:40.sourceText: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
22:40.targetText: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:41.sourceText: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς
22:41.targetText: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:

groups.note: The genitive absolute Συνηγμένων … τῶν Φαρισαίων supplies While.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

22:42.sourceText: λέγων Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ; τίνος υἱός ἐστιν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Τοῦ Δαυείδ.
22:42.targetText: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?”  “David’s,” they answered.

22:43.targetText: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says:

groups.note: The participle λέγων ("saying") is rendered he says.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker, who is only the subject of λέγει here.

22:44.sourceText: Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου;
22:44.targetText: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

22:45.sourceText: εἰ οὖν Δαυεὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν Κύριον, πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν;
22:45.targetText: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered with the name.

22:46.sourceText: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ λόγον, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπ’ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι.
